units.text: Your next decade brings a will that refuses to give once you decide something is yours to protect. The same hold pushes back people who meant to help, and you choose which stands are worth taking.

In this decade a fierce, guarding will runs through what you do, and you hold your ground where others give way. People who push against it meet a wall, and what you want under it is to keep your own people safe.
A year with this guest gives you a harder edge whenever something of yours comes under threat. You stand firm faster than usual, and the people near you feel the push of it.
You guard what is yours and refuse to bend.
This decade hardens your will around the things you protect.

From your mid-thirties your home carries a fierce, guarding will, and you stand in front of the people you live with. The same will pushes a partner back in a disagreement, because you hold a line long after it has stopped mattering. What you want under it is a home nobody can take from you.

Your Home Chapter made you the one who stood guard over the household. You held firm when the house was pushed, and a partner met the same firmness over small things as often as large ones. Today you know which of those stands at home earned their cost.

Your Home Chapter runs on a will that guards the people under your roof. Since your mid-thirties you hold your ground in every disagreement at home, and a partner feels the push as distance. You are at your best here when the stand you take protects someone rather than a point.

From your late forties a fierce will gathers around what you have built and the people after you. You defend both hard, and younger people who want to try their own way meet a wall where they hoped for a gate. Your strength in these years lies in picking the few stands that protect them.

Your Late Chapter gave you a guarding will that bent for nobody. You stood between the people after you and whatever pressed on them, and some of them found it hard to argue their own case with you. What you carry from those years is a clear sense of which stands mattered.

In your Late Chapter your will has a hard, protective edge, and you hold to what you have built. The people after you lean on that strength and also bump against it when they want to change things. You choose your stands with more care now, and the ones you take carry real weight.

Your Rising Chapter brings a hard, guarding will into work and study. Colleagues find you immovable once you take a position, and fewer of them bring you their doubts. You do your best work in these years on the stands that protect your own.

Through your twenties you held your ground at work and in study, and nobody moved you once you had decided. That firmness kept your own work safe, and it also pushed back friends and colleagues who wanted a say. You still carry the will, along with a sharper eye for when it helps.

Your Rising Chapter carries a will with a hard edge, and you defend your work and your friends without being asked. The cost is plain, since colleagues stop arguing with you and their doubts never reach you. You hold the line because you want to protect what is yours.

Your Early Chapter gave you a stubborn, protective streak in the first home. As a child you dug in over the things you saw as yours, and the adults around you met a will that did not bend easily. You still carry that guard, now with a choice about where you place it.

At home and at school you guard what you see as yours, and you refuse to give way once you dig in. Other children and the adults around you feel that push. You are strongest when the thing you defend is a friend or a fair turn.
Your next decade sharpens your nerve for a chance, and you move before the moment closes. Work you start fast goes out unmarked, and you gain most when your name travels with it.

This decade gives you a quick hand for the chance in front of you, and you take it while others weigh it up. The speed leaves your work open for anyone to claim, and what you want is the chance before it shuts.

In a year this guest visits, you see a chance and close on it before most people have looked up. Credit for what you start goes to whoever speaks first, and you hold on to more of it by marking your work early.
You take the chance before anyone else has decided.
This decade quickens your hand on every chance that passes.

From your mid-thirties your home life moves at your speed, and you settle where to live before a partner has finished thinking. The quickness wins you good chances at home. It also leaves a partner feeling the decision was made without them, and you do best when you bring them in at the start.

Your Home Chapter ran fast. You took chances on the house, the move and the shape of your home before a partner had weighed them, and some of those quick calls were the best you made. You carry the same nerve still, and you know now how much a partner wanted a say.

Since your mid-thirties your home runs on quick decisions, and you act on a good chance for the household the day it shows itself. A partner who needs longer feels left behind by that pace. Your gift here is speed, and it serves you best on the choices you make together.

From your late forties your eye for a good chance stays quick, and you still move faster than people half your age. The work you begin in these years passes to others to finish, and the credit passes with it. You are at your strongest in the later years when the people after you know whose idea it was.

Your Late Chapter kept you quick on a chance long after others had slowed down. You started more than you finished, and the people after you took much of it forward under their own names. What stays with you is the nerve, and the pleasure of having moved first.

In your Late Chapter you still see a chance first and act before others have weighed it. You hand much of what you start to the people after you, and your part in it goes unnamed unless you put it there. You care more about moving first than about finishing.

Your Rising Chapter brings a hand that closes on a chance before it slips past. In first jobs and study you move early, and unmarked work passes under someone else's name. You move fastest of anyone around you in these years.

Through your twenties you took chances at work while friends and colleagues were still making up their minds. Some of your best early work went out without your name and came back as someone else's. You still carry that fast nerve, and you mark what you make now.

Your Early Chapter gave you a quick hand at school and at home, and you grabbed a chance before anyone else in your first home had noticed it. Ideas you came up with were often credited to an older relative or a classmate. You kept the speed, and it serves you still.

At school and at home you spot a chance and take it before the others have decided. Classmates who speak first end up with credit for your ideas, and that stings. You are the first to move in your class, and that speed belongs to you.

Your next decade deepens the part of your thinking that nobody else sees, and your plans run several moves past what you show. People close to you hear of your choices late, and you decide who sees the whole of you.

In this decade you think further than you let on, and you keep your real plan to yourself until it is ready. The people nearest you learn of it last, and you guard that privacy because being fully seen feels unsafe.
A year with this guest turns your thinking inward and long, and you plan well past what anyone can see. Those close to you find out late, and you choose how much of the plan to show them.
You think several moves further than you show.
This decade sharpens the strategy you keep behind your face.

From your mid-thirties your home holds a mind that plans far past what it shows. A partner hears your thinking late, at times after the choice is already made, and that gap reads as distance. Your safety lies in staying partly unseen, and home works best for you when one person sees all of it.

Your Home Chapter ran on plans you kept close. You thought far past what a partner saw, and the household heard your decisions after they were already made. You carry that strategic mind still, along with a clearer sense of who gets to see it.

Since your mid-thirties your thinking at home runs deeper than anything you say about it. A partner learns of your plans late and reads the silence as a closed door. What you want is the safety of not being fully seen, and the house steadies when you let one person past the mask.

From your late forties your mind runs a long game in later work, and you see several steps further than you show. The people after you hear your reasons late, and some of what you know stays with you unshared. You choose in these years who sees the whole plan.

Your Late Chapter gave your thinking its longest reach. You planned far past what you showed, and the people after you learned your reasons late or pieced them together alone. What you hold from those years is a strategist's mind and a careful hand with who sees it.

In your Late Chapter your mind works further on than anyone around you guesses. The people after you hear your plans late and learn your reasons last. You stay partly hidden by choice, and the few who know all of it are the ones you picked.

Your Rising Chapter brings a mind that plans well past what it shows, at work and in study. Colleagues and friends hear your thinking late, often after you have already moved. You are at your sharpest in these years on work that rewards a quiet, long plan.

Through your twenties you kept your real plans behind a calm face at work and in study. Friends and colleagues heard what you meant to do only once it was done. You still carry that strategic streak, and you know who you let see past it.

Your Rising Chapter carries a strategist's mind, and you think three moves past what you show at work. Friends and colleagues hear your plans late and feel left out of them. You feel safest partly unseen, and you pick who sees the rest.

Your Early Chapter gave you a private, planning mind in the first home. As a child you thought further than you said, and the adults around you found out what you had worked out long after you had. That hidden depth is still yours, and you show it to whom you choose.

At school and at home your mind runs further than what you say, and you keep your plans quiet until they are ready. The adults around you hear about them late. You feel safest when not everything about you is on view.
